intuition: Copy a path list for every child and retain all partial paths. A shared path avoids those repeated intermediate copies. Partial root paths are shared by sibling branches, so copying them at every descent stores repeated ancestry unnecessarily.

Maintain one path list for the current recursive branch. A node is appended on entry, and removed after its descendants finish. Only a node with neither child completes a requested path. Joining the list at that moment captures a stable string before backtracking changes working storage. A node with one child must continue downward; stopping there would report an internal prefix rather than a root-to-leaf path. Output strings can repeat when distinct leaves have equal value sequences, and those occurrences must be preserved.

On entering a node, path contains exactly its ancestors. Appending the current value creates its complete root path. Only leaves produce results, and DFS reaches each leaf once. Popping restores the ancestor path for sibling exploration, so all and only root-to-leaf paths are emitted. L is the total number of characters in all returned paths; joining at leaves accounts for output size.

steps: Descend left to 2, then its right child 5, producing ["1","2","5"].
Pop 5 and 2 while returning, leaving the root path ["1"].
Visit right leaf 3 and record "1->3"; return both strings.
